simple.meaning: שׁוּנַמִּית (Shûwnammîyth) is a Hebrew word meaning “a Shunammitess , or female inhabitant of Shunem.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שׁוּנַמִּית (H7767) appears 8 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 1:3, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Kings.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שׁוּנַמִּית (H7767) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שׁוּנַמִּית (H7767) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שׁוּנַמִּית (Shûwnammîyth) / H7767 is traced through 1 Kings 1:3, 1 Kings 1:15, 1 Kings 2:17, 1 Kings 2:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

structuredEvidence.definition: a Shunammitess , or female inhabitant of Shunem

firstOccurrence.englishText: So they sought for a beautiful young lady throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

timeline.evidenceText: So they sought for a beautiful young lady throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
Bathsheba went in to the king in his room. The king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.
He said, “Please speak to Solomon the king (for he will not tell you ‘no’), that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.”
She said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as wife.”

King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingdom also; for he is my elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.”
He said to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” When he had called her, she stood before him.
So she went, and came to the man of God to Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her afar off, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, there is the Shunammite.
He called Gehazi, and said, “Call this Shunammite!” So he called her.
